title: Unit – 5 : Session – 8 : SLO – 2  |  ARM CPSR, Modes and Software Interrupts
sections: 1. MRS — MRS Rd, CPSR moves the status register (including mode bits) into a general register.
2. Supervisor (SVC) — SWI triggers a software interrupt that enters Supervisor mode.
3. R8 — FIQ mode banks registers R8–R14.
1. TRUE — FIQ banks R8–R14 (7 registers) vs IRQ's R13–R14 (2), so FIQ handlers avoid stacking overhead.
2. FALSE — the CONTROL register belongs to ARMv7-M (Cortex-M); ARMv7-A switches modes via CPSR writes/exceptions.
3. TRUE — SWI is precisely the User → Supervisor transition mechanism (system calls).
1. 5 — CPSR mode bits M[4:0] determine the processor mode.
3. 2 — IRQ banks only R13_irq and R14_irq.
